title: Bing Crosby with the Whiteman band
summary: He remembers Bing as ambitious, musical and funny, recalls the Rhythm Boys' start, and says Crosby drew on Jolson, Bix and Louis.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: What about Bing? What are you reminiscences of Bing?
In what way? Oh Bing was great.
Being around him with the Whiteman band.

Bing's a fine guy. He was ambitious but not -- I don't think he wanted to stay in the band too long. Rinker and I was pretty close friends. Well, Bing and I were too and Al describes the two of them as singers of fast songs.

I said, "What did you do before you got with Paul?" "We were singers of fast songs." Vaudeville jobs, up and down the coast. They said they played all the circuits out there and then Paul picked them up and I guess they were a bust until he brought [Harry] Barris in and then they were a hit right off.
Barris, I guess, of course, wrote some great songs.
Yeah, well, Bing helped him with his lyrics, I think, but Bing was -- he was a great performer.

Particularly in recording. I remember 'Taint So, Honey,' one of Willard Robison's things. I wanted to -- I don't know why, I wanted to start it off with a vocal, just a prank sort of, without any introduction, so I just gave him the note he starts on. He knew the song, got to know the song (sings), that's the verse and I wanted him to sing the verse. Well, I just gave him the note and I think Paul beat off, or I did, well, anyway, he came right in and sang it. No problems like that, or anything.

And no problems with changes of key. He was a very musical guy, had a wonderful ear and then he was a lot of fun, a lot of laughs, makes with the big words, liked to do that. I think he must have written a lot of the script or helped those guys, because when I'd hear him on the air, he was that way around -- very, very normal and natural. Doing what came naturally.
You would say he was influenced by the jazz music of that period in his singing.

Oh, yeah, he knew a good band when he heard one. Good musicians, he understood -- he was a good jazz man, that's all there was to it. Good singer. What, he was a former drummer had a good sense of rhythm. In my opinion -- shouldn't be opinionated -- I think if you listen to Bing, I think you will find he got a lot of his stuff but modernized it at his age, from Jolson.
You think musicians like Louis and
Bix influenced him too, would you say.
Because they influenced everybody, I guess.

That's right. They were right up in the top and they were standards to go by. I remember in this Old Miss Hannah, he had to do a vocal in Old Miss Hannah, and the way he got into it, he was just supposed to start on Old Miss Hannah, (sings) he goes into something like that and it just worked out beautifully. He had excellent taste.
That's the way I say about these guys, they had excellent taste. Bix, fine, fine taste and Bing the same way. And Trumbauer.
